body.statement:
Fix \(t\in[0,1]\) and let
\[
 E=\{(\delta_D,\delta_S)\in\mathcal B:\Theta_I(q;\delta_D,\delta_S)\neq\varnothing\}.
\]
The robust region \(\mathcal R_t\) is relatively downward closed on \(E\): if two budget pairs are coordinatewise ordered, the larger lies in \(\mathcal R_t\), and the smaller belongs to \(E\), then the smaller lies in \(\mathcal R_t\). If \(q\) is rational, a finite semialgebraic refinement of the rational endpoint chart separately labels model-infeasible, model-feasible/target-empty, and target-nonempty pieces, the falsification boundary, the positive-\(H\) target-existence boundary, the equality locus \(L=t\), and the actual relative conclusion boundary
\[
 \partial_E\mathcal R_t
 =\overline{\mathcal R_t}^{E}
  \cap\overline{E\setminus\mathcal R_t}^{E}.
\]
A refined piece receives the conclusion-boundary label only when it is contained in \(\partial_E\mathcal R_t\), equivalently when every relative \(E\)-neighborhood of every retained point meets both \(\mathcal R_t\) and \(E\setminus\mathcal R_t\). An \(L=t\) plateau is retained in the equality locus but is not a conclusion-boundary piece unless this pointwise condition holds; coincident lower-dimensional pieces may carry every valid label. Along every declared radial path, \(\mathcal F_\gamma\), \(\mathcal E_\gamma\), and \(\mathcal B_{\gamma,t}\) are upward closed. If \(\mathcal E_\gamma=\varnothing\), the target never exists and breakdown is inapplicable; if \(\mathcal B_{\gamma,t}=\varnothing\), no breakdown occurs on the path; and \(\lambda_{\rm crit}=\lambda_{\rm tar}\) with \(\iota_{\rm crit}=0\) means failure occurs immediately after, but not at, target entry. When \(q\), \(\bar{\boldsymbol\delta}\), and \(t\) are rational, intersecting the finite chart with \(\gamma_{\bar{\boldsymbol\delta}}\) and applying rational univariate root isolation gives exact finite values of \(\lambda_{\rm feas}\), \(\lambda_{\rm tar}\), \(\lambda_{\rm crit}\), \(\iota_{\rm crit}\), and \(\Delta_{\rm crit}\) when the latter is defined; no scalable or output-sensitive complexity claim is made.
body.justification: The result separates model entry, target entry, equality loci, and genuine conclusion failure, and reports the first failure along a declared joint-relaxation path.
body.gap: A survivor-complier denominator creates a separate target-entry frontier. Moreover, \(L=t\) alone identifies an equality locus, not a conclusion boundary: every retained boundary point must have robust and target-existing nonrobust points in every relative neighborhood.
body.consumer: A Job Corps or Oregon analyst can report model-entry, target-entry, critical-budget, and attainment diagnostics without treating an empty target or an interior equality plateau as evidence of robustness.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(q\). For a full law with \(H>0\), the causal parameter is \(\theta=N/H\). By \(\mathrm{thm:projection\text{-}lifting}\), the observed-law functional \(\Theta_I(q;\delta_D,\delta_S)\) is exactly the set of these causal values over compatible full laws. By \(\mathrm{def:endpoints}\), \(L\) is defined only when that set is nonempty. Thus, on \(E\), \(L\geq t\) is equivalent to the causal conclusion that every compatible survivor-complier strict-benefit probability is at least \(t\); it does not define the causal probability.

Let \(\boldsymbol\delta^-=(\delta_D^-,\delta_S^-)\) and \(\boldsymbol\delta^+=(\delta_D^+,\delta_S^+)\) satisfy \(\boldsymbol\delta^-\leq\boldsymbol\delta^+\) coordinatewise. If \(z\in Q_o(q,\boldsymbol\delta^-)\), every nonbudget constraint is unchanged at \(\boldsymbol\delta^+\), while
\[
 \sum_x f_x\leq\delta_D^-\leq\delta_D^+
\]
and, using \(c_x\geq0\),
\[
 \sum_x\{o_xU_x+(1-o_x)V_x-h_x\}
 \leq\delta_S^-\sum_xc_x
 \leq\delta_S^+\sum_xc_x.
\]
Therefore
\[
 Q_o(q,\boldsymbol\delta^-)
 \subseteq Q_o(q,\boldsymbol\delta^+),
 \qquad
 \Theta_I(q;\boldsymbol\delta^-)
 \subseteq\Theta_I(q;\boldsymbol\delta^+).
\]
If \(\boldsymbol\delta^-\in E\) and \(\boldsymbol\delta^+\in\mathcal R_t\), endpoint attainment gives
\[
 L(q;\boldsymbol\delta^-)
 \geq L(q;\boldsymbol\delta^+)
 \geq t,
\]
so \(\boldsymbol\delta^-\in\mathcal R_t\). Initial model infeasibility or target emptiness is excluded, not counted as robustness.

Assume now that \(q\) is rational. By \(\mathrm{thm:finite\text{-}rational\text{-}charts}\), every chart stratum has exactly one of the three feasibility/target labels. On a target-nonempty stratum \(\mathcal S_j\), write
\[
 L(q;\delta_D,\delta_S)
 =\frac{A_j(\delta_D,\delta_S)}{B_j(\delta_D,\delta_S)},
 \qquad B_j\neq0\text{ on }\mathcal S_j,
\]
with rational polynomials \(A_j,B_j\). Refine by the sign \(\sigma_j\in\{-1,1\}\) of \(B_j\). Then
\[
 L\geq t
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \sigma_j(A_j-tB_j)\geq0.
\]
Thus \(E\), \(\mathcal R_t\), and \(E\setminus\mathcal R_t\) are finite unions of semialgebraic sign pieces. Model-infeasible and target-empty pieces are outside \(E\).

Apply \(\mathrm{lem:finite-frontier-compatible-sign-refinement}\) to the finite polynomial list defining the chart, the denominators, the polynomials \(A_j-tB_j\), and the facets of \(\mathcal B\). Restrict its cells to \(E\), which gives the relative topology used below. Define, as asserted,
\[
 \partial_E\mathcal R_t
 =\overline{\mathcal R_t}^{E}
  \cap\overline{E\setminus\mathcal R_t}^{E}.
\]
The lemma refines this intersection into finitely many whole cells. A retained cell \(C\) is labeled a conclusion-boundary piece exactly when
\[
 C\subseteq\partial_E\mathcal R_t.
\]
By the definition of relative closure, this is equivalent to the pointwise condition
\[
 \text{for every }\delta\in C\text{ and every relative }E\text{-neighborhood }G\ni\delta,
 \quad
 G\cap\mathcal R_t\neq\varnothing
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 G\cap(E\setminus\mathcal R_t)\neq\varnothing.
\]
This is strictly stronger than asking only whether \(\overline C^{E}\) meets both sides. On a target-nonempty cell,
\[
 A_j-tB_j=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad L=t,
\]
so this equation certifies the equality locus only. If it holds throughout a plateau lying in the relative interior of \(\mathcal R_t\), some relative neighborhood is wholly robust; hence the plateau is not in \(\partial_E\mathcal R_t\). The same conclusion covers a forced \(\Theta_I=\{1\}\) plateau at \(t=1\). Interfaces between model-infeasible and model-feasible cells receive the falsification-boundary label, and interfaces within the model-feasible set between target-empty and target-nonempty cells receive the positive-\(H\) target-existence label. The refinement retains intersections, so a lower-dimensional cell may carry several labels when each defining condition holds.

Fix \(\bar{\boldsymbol\delta}\in\mathcal B\setminus\{\boldsymbol0\}\). For \(0\leq\lambda_0\leq\lambda_1\leq1\), nonnegativity of both coordinates of \(\bar{\boldsymbol\delta}\) gives
\[
 \gamma_{\bar{\boldsymbol\delta}}(\lambda_0)
 \leq\gamma_{\bar{\boldsymbol\delta}}(\lambda_1)
\]
coordinatewise. Branch expansion proved above makes \(\mathcal F_\gamma\) upward closed. Restricting the inclusion to \(H>0\) makes \(\mathcal E_\gamma\) upward closed. If \(\lambda_0\in\mathcal B_{\gamma,t}\), identified-set inclusion and endpoint attainment yield
\[
 L(q;\gamma_{\bar{\boldsymbol\delta}}(\lambda_1))
 \leq L(q;\gamma_{\bar{\boldsymbol\delta}}(\lambda_0))<t,
\]
and target existence persists, so \(\mathcal B_{\gamma,t}\) is upward closed.

The interpretations now follow from the definitions. If \(\mathcal E_\gamma=\varnothing\), no path point admits the causal target. If \(\mathcal B_{\gamma,t}=\varnothing\), no target-existing path point violates the conclusion. Suppose \(\mathcal B_{\gamma,t}\neq\varnothing\), put \(a=\lambda_{\rm crit}\), and assume \(a=\lambda_{\rm tar}\) but \(\iota_{\rm crit}=0\). For every \(\lambda>a\), the definition of the infimum supplies \(b\in\mathcal B_{\gamma,t}\) with \(a<b<\lambda\); upward closure gives \(\lambda\in\mathcal B_{\gamma,t}\). At \(a\) there is no failure. Thus failure occurs immediately after, but not at, target entry. If \(a\leq1\), then \(\Delta_{\rm crit}=\gamma_{\bar{\boldsymbol\delta}}(a)\), and \(\iota_{\rm crit}\) records whether that budget pair itself is a failure point.

Finally suppose \(q\), \(\bar{\boldsymbol\delta}\), and \(t\) are rational. Substitute
\[
 (\delta_D,\delta_S)=\gamma_{\bar{\boldsymbol\delta}}(\lambda)
\]
in every chart and conclusion-sign polynomial. The result is a finite family of univariate rational polynomials. The exact rational root-isolation construction in \(\mathrm{lem:finite-frontier-compatible-sign-refinement}\) partitions \([0,1]\) into algebraic points and open intervals on which every sign and label is constant. Testing one exact sample per interval and the isolated roots themselves determines \(\mathcal F_\gamma\), \(\mathcal E_\gamma\), and \(\mathcal B_{\gamma,t}\), including endpoint inclusion. Their infima, \(\iota_{\rm crit}\), and \(\Delta_{\rm crit}\) when defined follow exactly. The enumeration is finite; no output-sensitive or scalable bound is used.
